text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Chancellor Helmut Kohl expected to announce by spring whether will stand in 1998 election. Decision to depend on success of planned tax and pension reforms.

- U.S. secretary of state Madeleine Albright stops off in Bonn as part of her first overseas trip since taking office in January. Due to meet Kohl and Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel for talks on NATO expansion, the peace process in the Middle East and the situation in the former Yugoslavia.
- Thousands of postal workers stage work stoppages in protest against a draft law that would remove the German post office's monopoly.
- As Bundesliga starts again, Bayern Munich hold onto their position at the top of the table with a 3-0 victory over St Pauli, fending off challenge from reigning champions Borussia Dortmund.
- A decision over whether nuclear energy will continued to be used in Germany not expected until 2005.
- German competition law due to be changed during this legislative period, following the recommendation of the monopoly commission.
HANDELSBLATT
- Opposition Social Democrats (SPD) parliamentary budget expert Karl Diller estimates a budget deficit of at least 10 billion marks due to higher unemployment benefit pay-outs and lower tax receipts.
- Ruling coalition partners set to decide on Tuesday whether employees must pay for the increased expenditure of health insurance funds in future.
- The semi-conductor market expected to grow again in 1997 after a weak last year.
- Metals and engineering union IG Metall fears that unemployment will rise to five million as long as the government remains commited to tight budget discipline.
- Spanish truck strike hits German car manufacturers, including Volkswagen AG and Opel .
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- German economic state secretary Johannes Ludewig, a close aide of Kohl, set to become new head of Deutsche Bahn, the German national railway, according to government sources.

- European Monetary Institute President Alexandre Lamfalussy says it is unlikely that European Union states will have brought their public finances under control by next spring when participants in planned monetary union should be decided.
- Postal workers set to continue protest against threat of removal of post office's monopoly. The postal workers union (DPG) calls a demonstration for around 10,000 in Bonn.
- A week before planned talks between the ruling coalition and the SPD on tax reform, both sides seen ready to compromise.
DIE WELT
- The government wants to cap payments to former cabinet ministers and state secretaries.
- New SPD debate on the ending of nuclear energy.
- Kohl comments over the weekend weighed up for any indication as to whether he will stand again in the 1998 election.
- Left-wing youths fight right-wing sympathisers in the eastern cities of Magdeburg, Brandenburg and Berlin. Several people injured.
- Protests mount ahead of planned transport of nuclear waste shipment to depot at Gorleben, near Hanover.
